doc.title: Houston Person Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Influences: R&B, gospel and the church
title: Growing up on rhythm and blues and country music
summary: Asked about his sound, Person names R&B artists such as Roy Milton, Amos Milburn and Charles Brown, and the vocal groups, who also used jazz players.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: You talked about them helping you form your conception. How do you feel that your voice on the tenor is different from other tenor players and other instrumentalists in general? Or what typifies your sound? What do you like?
I like all kinds of music. I grew up with rhythm & blues and country & western music.
Who were some of your favorite rhythm & blues artists?

Roy Milton, Amos Milburn, Bull Moose Jackson. They all use jazz players, so it wasn’t such finely drawn lines as there are now. Oh, man there were so many. Charles Brown. And most of these artists, you know, could be considered jazz artists also. The Ravens, The Dominoes, and all those, Sonny Till and the Orioles. So it was a lot of them, of that type. Of course there was Gospel music which I was greatly influenced by. So it’s a whole cross section of a lot of things.
You know basically they say that the only difference between rhythm & blues and Gospel is one guy is talking about God and the other one is talking about his girlfriend.
